qt: to the Commission Anna Bryłka (PfE) Subject:

In Poland, the ARiMR payment agency is challenging aid granted to agricultural producer groups, citing ‘artificially created conditions’, including personal, family, organisational or economic links between producers. In some cases, the structures in question had previously been operating with the authority’s knowledge, and the aid was granted following an inspection. In its Judgment of 12 September 2013 in Case C-434/12, Slancheva sila EOOD, the CJEU stated that a finding of artificially created conditions requires consideration of both objective and subjective elements and an assessment of all the circumstances of the specific case. 1.

Can legal, economic, functional or personal links, including family ties, be sufficient in themselves to establish that the conditions for obtaining aid were artificially created, without demonstrating both the objective and subjective elements required by the caselaw of the CJEU?

Does EU law permit – and under what conditions – the recovery of aid previously granted and paid out, where an authority subsequently makes a different assessment of the same circumstances of which it was already aware at the time the aid was granted, without demonstrating that the beneficiaries’ primary objective was to obtain an advantage contrary to the purpose of the support scheme?
What is the significance, in such cases, of the principles of legal certainty, the protection of legitimate expectations, proportionality and the individual assessment of the case?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (21.10.2026) In its judgment in case C-434/121, the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) held that the conditions for the application of the concept of ‘artificially created conditions’ under Article 4(8) of Regulation No 65/20112 require both an objective and a subjective element. When assessing the latter, legal, economic and/or personal links can be taken into account. The Court also held in the same judgment that there must be objective evidence of the intent to exclusively obtain an advantage contrary to the objectives of the support scheme by artificially creating the conditions required for payment3. The same concept of ‘artificially created conditions’ has been enshrined in Article 62 of Regulation (EU) 2021/21164. As regards the general principles of legal certainty, the protection of legitimate expectations and proportionality, they should be taken into account in the case-by-case analysis that needs to be carried out by the national authorities.
